documentTitle: SERA — Standardised European Rules of the Air, Regulation (EU) 923/2012
closureReason: manifested windows are landed, but high-priority source-window hardening remains outside current package scope

sections.notes: SERA.8015(e) Read-back of clearances and safety-related information. Compact regulatory text: four numbered sub-paragraphs (1)-(4) with the always-read-back list (i)-(iv) nested under (1).

SERA.8005 Operation of air traffic control service. Three top-level paragraphs (a/b/c): (a) what an ATC unit shall do (4 numbered duties); (b) which classes of flight separation must be provided between (5 numbered cases plus exception); (c) separation methods (vertical / horizontal with sub-cases). Clean clause hierarchy.
SERA.8010 Separation minima. Compact: (a) ANSP selects minima; (b) coordination between neighbouring airspaces; (c) notification of minima to ATS units and pilots.

SERA.8015 Air traffic control clearances paragraphs (a)-(d): (a) basis of clearances, (b) operation subject to clearance with sub-numbered cases, (c) potential reclearance, (d) contents of clearances (5 numbered fields). The (e) readback paragraph already covered separately as readback_8015_e.
SERA.8015(f) Coordination of clearances: route coverage, downstream clearances, and controlled-airspace scope. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.
SERA.8020 Adherence to flight plan: controlled-flight adherence, amended clearance, emergency deviation, and requested change content. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.
SERA.8025 Position reports: controlled-flight reporting duty and data-link exception. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.
SERA.8030 Termination of control: duty to advise ATC when no longer subject to ATC service. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.
SERA.8035 Communications: continuous voice watch, two-way communication as necessary, CPDLC persistence, and comms-failure reference. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.

sourceUnits.claimText: Requests for flight plan changes involving a change of route with destination changed shall include aircraft identification, flight rules, description of revised route of flight to revised destination aerodrome including related flight plan data, beginning with the position from which requested change of route is to commence, revised time estimates, alternate aerodrome(s), and any other pertinent information.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specific data content requirement for flight plan change requests regarding route changes with changed destination.
exactSourceQuotes: (c) Intended changes. Requests for flight plan changes shall include information as indicated hereunder:

(ii) Destination changed: aircraft identification; flight rules; description of revised route of flight to revised desti­
nation aerodrome including related flight plan data, beginning with the position from which requested change
of route is to commence; revised time estimates; alternate aerodrome(s); any other pertinent information.

curationApplied.reasoning: Promoted SERA.8020(c)(2)(ii) destination-changed flight-plan-change content rule with the governing parent clause and the verbatim hyphenated source text.

manualRepair.reasoning: Promoted SERA.8020(c)(2)(ii) destination-changed flight-plan-change content rule with the governing parent clause and the verbatim hyphenated source text.

sourceUnits.claimText: An aircraft shall adhere to the current flight plan or the applicable portion of a current flight plan submitted for a controlled flight unless a request for a change has been made and clearance obtained from the appropriate air traffic control unit, or unless an emergency situation arises which necessitates immediate action by the aircraft.
sourceUnits.rationale: Core adherence obligation with explicit exceptions for amended clearances and emergencies.
exactSourceQuotes: an aircraft shall adhere to the current flight plan or the applicable portion of a current flight plan submitted for a controlled flight unless a request for a change has been made and clearance obtained from the appropriate air traffic control unit, or unless an emergency situation arises which necessitates immediate action by the aircraft

sourceUnits.claimText: When flight in VMC in accordance with its current flight plan will not be practicable, a VFR flight operated as a controlled flight shall request clearance to operate in accordance with the instrument flight rules.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specific action requirement for VFR flights to transition to IFR when VMC is no longer practicable.
exactSourceQuotes: request clearance to operate in accordance with the instrument flight rules

sourceUnits.claimText: If the average true airspeed at cruising level varies or is expected to vary by plus or minus 5 per cent from that given in the flight plan, the appropriate air traffic services unit shall be so informed.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandatory notification requirement for significant true airspeed variations.
exactSourceQuotes: if the average true airspeed at cruising level between reporting points varies or is expected to vary by plus or minus 5 per cent of the true airspeed, from that given in the flight plan, the appropriate air traffic services unit shall be so informed

sourceUnits.claimText: If operated within a control zone, a VFR flight operated as a controlled flight shall request authorisation to operate as a special VFR flight when flight in VMC in accordance with its current flight plan will not be practicable.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specific action requirement for VFR flights within control zones encountering weather deterioration.
exactSourceQuotes: if operated within a control zone, request authorisation to operate as a special VFR flight

sourceUnits.claimText: When flight in VMC in accordance with its current flight plan will not be practicable, a VFR flight operated as a controlled flight shall request an amended clearance enabling the aircraft to continue in VMC to destination or to an alternative aerodrome, or to leave the airspace within which an ATC clearance is required.
sourceUnits.rationale: Primary action requirement for VFR flights encountering weather deterioration below VMC.
exactSourceQuotes: request an amended clearance enabling the aircraft to continue in VMC to destination or to an alternative aerodrome, or to leave the airspace within which an ATC clearance is required

sourceUnits.claimText: Controlled flights on an established ATS route shall, in so far as practicable, operate along the defined centre line of that route unless otherwise authorised or directed.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specific lateral navigation requirement for established ATS routes.
exactSourceQuotes: controlled flights shall, in so far as practicable: (i) when on an established ATS route, operate along the defined centre line of that route

sourceUnits.claimText: Requests for flight plan changes involving a change of cruising level shall include aircraft identification, requested new cruising level and cruising speed at this level, and revised time estimates (when applicable) at subsequent flight information region boundaries.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specific data content requirement for flight plan change requests regarding cruising level.
exactSourceQuotes: Change of cruising level: aircraft identification; requested new cruising level and cruising speed at this level, revised time estimates (when applicable) at subsequent flight information region boundaries

sourceUnits.claimText: If the time estimate for the next applicable reporting point, flight information region boundary or destination aerodrome is in error in excess of 3 minutes (or other prescribed period), a revised estimated time shall be notified as soon as possible to the appropriate air traffic services unit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandatory notification requirement for significant time estimate errors.
exactSourceQuotes: if the time estimate for the next applicable reporting point, flight information region boundary or destination aerodrome, whichever comes first, is found to be in error in excess of 3 minutes from that notified to air traffic services, or such other period of time as is prescribed by the competent authority or on the basis of ICAO regional air navigation agreements, a revised estimated time shall be notified as soon as possible to the appropriate air traffic services unit

sourceUnits.claimText: After exercising emergency authority, the appropriate air traffic services unit shall be notified of the action taken and that this action has been taken under emergency authority as soon as circumstances permit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandatory notification obligation following the exercise of emergency authority.
exactSourceQuotes: as soon as circumstances permit, after such emergency authority is exercised, the appropriate air traffic services unit shall be notified of the action taken and that this action has been taken under emergency authority

sourceUnits.claimText: Deviation from the VOR changeover requirements shall be notified to the appropriate air traffic services unit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandatory notification requirement for deviations from specific navigation guidance rules.
exactSourceQuotes: Deviation from the requirements in (2) shall be notified to the appropriate air traffic services unit

sourceUnits.claimText: An aircraft operating along an ATS route segment defined by VOR shall change over for its primary navigation guidance from the facility behind the aircraft to that ahead of it at, or as close as operationally feasible to, the changeover point, where established, unless otherwise authorised or directed.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandatory procedure for VOR navigation changeover points.
exactSourceQuotes: an aircraft operating along an ATS route segment defined by reference to very high frequency omnidirectional radio ranges shall change over for its primary navigation guidance from the facility behind the aircraft to that ahead of it at, or as close as operationally feasible to, the changeover point, where established

sourceUnits.claimText: If no clearance in accordance with (a) can be obtained, a VFR flight operated as a controlled flight shall continue to operate in VMC and notify the appropriate ATC unit of the action being taken either to leave the airspace concerned or to land at the nearest suitable aerodrome.
sourceUnits.rationale: Fallback action requirement for VFR flights when amended clearance cannot be obtained.
exactSourceQuotes: if no clearance in accordance with a) can be obtained, continue to operate in VMC and notify the appropriate ATC unit of the action being taken either to leave the airspace concerned or to land at the nearest suitable aerodrome

sourceUnits.claimText: Requests for flight plan changes involving a change of route with destination unchanged shall include aircraft identification, flight rules, description of new route of flight including related flight plan data beginning with the position from which requested change of route is to commence, revised time estimates, and any other pertinent information.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specific data content requirement for flight plan change requests regarding route changes with unchanged destination.
exactSourceQuotes: Destination unchanged: aircraft identification; flight rules; description of new route of flight including related flight plan data beginning with the position from which requested change of route is to commence; revised time estimates; any other pertinent information

sourceUnits.claimText: When an ADS-C agreement is in place, the air traffic services unit shall be informed automatically via data link whenever changes occur beyond the threshold values stipulated by the ADS-C event contract.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandatory automated notification requirement for ADS-C event contract thresholds.
exactSourceQuotes: when an ADS-C agreement is in place, the air traffic services unit shall be informed automatically via data link whenever changes occur beyond the threshold values stipulated by the ADS-C event contract

sourceUnits.claimText: If a controlled flight inadvertently deviates from track, action shall be taken forthwith to adjust the heading of the aircraft to regain track as soon as practicable.
sourceUnits.rationale: Immediate corrective action requirement for inadvertent track deviations.
exactSourceQuotes: if the aircraft is off track, action shall be taken forthwith to adjust the heading of the aircraft to regain track as soon as practicable

sourceUnits.claimText: Controlled flights on any route other than an established ATS route shall, in so far as practicable, operate directly between the navigation facilities and/or points defining that route unless otherwise authorised or directed.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specific lateral navigation requirement for non-established ATS routes.
exactSourceQuotes:
(1) Unless otherwise authorised by the competent authority, or directed by the appropriate air traffic control unit,
controlled flights shall, in so far as practicable:
(ii) when on any other route, operate directly between the navigation facilities and/or points defining that route.

curationApplied.reasoning: Promoted SERA.8020(a)(1)(ii) non-ATS-route adherence rule after adding the governing unless-authorised/directed parent clause and the verbatim item text.

manualRepair.reasoning: Promoted SERA.8020(a)(1)(ii) non-ATS-route adherence rule after adding the governing unless-authorised/directed parent clause and the verbatim item text.

sourceUnits.claimText: Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation between IFR flights and VFR flights in airspace Class C.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(b)(3) defining separation obligation between IFR and VFR in Class C.
exactSourceQuotes: (b) Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation:
(3) between IFR flights and VFR flights in airspace Class C;

sourceUnits.claimText: Separation by an air traffic control unit shall be obtained by horizontal separation, specifically lateral separation, by maintaining aircraft on different routes or in different geographical areas.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(c)(2)(ii) defining lateral separation method.
exactSourceQuotes: (c) Except for cases when a reduction in separation minima in the vicinity of aerodromes can be applied, separation by an air traffic control unit shall be obtained by at least one of the following:
(2) horizontal separation, obtained by providing:
(ii) lateral separation, by maintaining aircraft on different routes or in different geographical areas.

sourceUnits.claimText: A flight may be cleared subject to maintaining own separation in respect of a specific portion of the flight below 3 050 m (10 000 ft) during climb or descent, during day in visual meteorological conditions, when requested by the pilot of an aircraft and agreed by the pilot of the other aircraft and if so prescribed by the competent authority for the cases listed under b) above in airspace Classes D and E.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative exception from SERA.8005(b) allowing reduced separation under specific conditions in Class D/E.
exactSourceQuotes: except that, when requested by the pilot of an aircraft and agreed by the pilot of the other aircraft and if so prescribed by the competent authority for the cases listed under b) above in airspace Classes D and E, a flight may be cleared subject to maintaining own separation in respect of a specific portion of the flight below 3 050 m (10 000 ft) during climb or descent, during day in visual meteorological conditions.

curationApplied.reasoning: The quote is verbatim and the claim accurately reflects the permissive exception in SERA.8005(b). Because the source uses “may,” the modality is correct, but under the authority floor table a may-statement cannot remain classified as authoritative_requirement and should be lowered one rung.

sourceUnits.claimText: Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation between all flights in airspace Classes A and B.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(b)(1) defining separation obligation in Class A/B.
exactSourceQuotes: (b) Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation:
(1) between all flights in airspace Classes A and B;

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control unit shall issue clearances and information for the purpose of preventing collision between aircraft under its control and of expediting and maintaining an orderly flow of traffic.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(a)(3) defining core operational output.
exactSourceQuotes: (3) issue clearances and information for the purpose of preventing collision between aircraft under its control and of expediting and maintaining an orderly flow of traffic;

sourceUnits.claimText: Separation by an air traffic control unit shall be obtained by vertical separation, obtained by assigning different levels selected from the table of cruising levels in Appendix 3 to the Annex to this Regulation, except that the correlation of levels to track as prescribed therein shall not apply whenever otherwise indicated in appropriate aeronautical information publications or air traffic control clearances. The vertical separation minimum shall be a nominal 300 m (1 000 ft) up to and including FL 410 and a nominal 600 m (2 000 ft) above this level.
sourceUnits.rationale: Unified claim from Attempt 1 keeping vertical separation definition and minima together as per source structure. Attempts 2 and 3 split these, which is less conservative for this specific logical block.
exactSourceQuotes: (c) Except for cases when a reduction in separation minima in the vicinity of aerodromes can be applied, separation by an air traffic control unit shall be obtained by at least one of the following:

(1) vertical separation, obtained by assigning different levels selected from the table of cruising levels in Appendix 3 to the Annex to this Regulation, except that the correlation of levels to track as prescribed therein shall not apply whenever otherwise indicated in appropriate aeronautical information publications or air traffic control clearances. The vertical separation minimum shall be a nominal 300 m (1 000 ft) up to and including FL 410 and a nominal 600 m (2 000 ft) above this level;

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control unit shall coordinate clearances with other units before transferring control of an aircraft to such other units.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(a)(4)(ii) specifying timing for mandatory coordination.
exactSourceQuotes: (4) coordinate clearances as necessary with other units:
(ii) before transferring control of an aircraft to such other units.

curationApplied.reasoning: The quoted source text verbatim supports this atomic SERA.8005(a)(4)(ii) requirement, with a shall-strength parent obligation applying to coordination before transfer of control. The bundle concern identifies a missing sibling condition under (i), but that does not make this candidate an unsupported umbrella or require changing its identity fields.

sourceUnits.claimText: Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation between IFR flights and special VFR flights.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(b)(4) defining separation obligation between IFR and SVFR.
exactSourceQuotes: (b) Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation:
(4) between IFR flights and special VFR flights;

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control unit shall determine from the information received, the relative positions of known aircraft to each other.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(a)(2) specifying situational awareness duty.
exactSourceQuotes: (2) determine from the information received, the relative positions of known aircraft to each other;

sourceUnits.claimText: Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation between IFR flights in airspace Classes C, D and E.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(b)(2) defining separation obligation for IFR in Class C/D/E.
exactSourceQuotes: (b) Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation:
(2) between IFR flights in airspace Classes C, D and E;

sourceUnits.claimText: Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation between special VFR flights unless otherwise prescribed by the competent authority.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(b)(5) defining separation obligation for SVFR.
exactSourceQuotes: (b) Clearances issued by air traffic control units shall provide separation:
(5) between special VFR flights unless otherwise prescribed by the competent authority;

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control unit shall coordinate clearances with other units whenever an aircraft might otherwise conflict with traffic operated under the control of such other units.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(a)(4)(i) specifying condition for mandatory coordination.
exactSourceQuotes: (4) coordinate clearances as necessary with other units:
(i) whenever an aircraft might otherwise conflict with traffic operated under the control of such other units;

curationApplied.reasoning: The claim is an atomic requirement supported verbatim by the cited parent and subordinate text, with correct shall modality and authoritative_requirement authority. The bundle objection is a structural artefact: the sibling accepted set already contains the parallel SERA.8005(a)(4)(ii) atomic requirement, so this item need not be rejected as incomplete.

sourceUnits.claimText: Separation by an air traffic control unit shall be obtained by horizontal separation, specifically longitudinal separation, by maintaining an interval between aircraft operating along the same, converging or reciprocal tracks, expressed in time or distance.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(c)(2)(i) defining longitudinal separation method.
exactSourceQuotes: (c) Except for cases when a reduction in separation minima in the vicinity of aerodromes can be applied, separation by an air traffic control unit shall be obtained by at least one of the following:
(2) horizontal separation, obtained by providing:
(i) longitudinal separation, by maintaining an interval between aircraft operating along the same, converging or reciprocal tracks, expressed in time or distance; or

curationApplied.reasoning: The quoted source text verbatim supports an authoritative shall requirement for longitudinal horizontal separation, using the parent operative clause in SERA.8005(c). The accepted lateral-separation sibling is complementary rather than redundant, and the candidate is an atomic item rather than an umbrella requiring rejection.

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control unit shall be provided with information on the intended movement of each aircraft, or variations therefrom, and with current information on the actual progress of each aircraft.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8005(a)(1) specifying data inputs.
exactSourceQuotes: (1) be provided with information on the intended movement of each aircraft, or variations therefrom, and with current information on the actual progress of each aircraft;

sourceUnits.claimText: When an aircraft intends to leave a control area for flight outside controlled airspace, and will subsequently reenter the same or another control area, a clearance from the point of departure to the aerodrome of first intended landing may be issued. Such clearance or revisions thereto shall apply only to those portions of the flight conducted within controlled airspace.
sourceUnits.rationale: Permissive rule for full clearances on flights exiting/entering controlled airspace.
exactSourceQuotes: When an aircraft intends to leave a control area for flight outside controlled airspace, and will subsequently reenter the same or another control area, a clearance from the point of departure to the aerodrome of first intended landing may be issued. Such clearance or revisions thereto shall apply only to those portions of the flight conducted within controlled airspace.

curationApplied.reasoning: The quoted text is verbatim and supports the claim, and it is not redundant with accepted siblings. The source provision combines a permissive issuance clause (“may be issued”) with a mandatory limitation (“shall apply only”), so the correct modality for this candidate is mixed, which is compatible with authoritative_requirement.

sourceUnits.claimText: A clearance issued as a downstream clearance shall be clearly identifiable as such to the pilot.
sourceUnits.rationale: Phraseology/identification requirement for downstream clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: A clearance issued as a downstream clearance shall be clearly identifiable as such to the pilot.

sourceUnits.claimText: When prescribed by the ATS unit, aircraft shall contact a downstream air traffic control unit, for the purpose of receiving a downstream clearance prior to the transfer of control point.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandatory action to contact downstream ATC when prescribed.
exactSourceQuotes: When prescribed by the ATS unit, aircraft shall contact a downstream air traffic control unit, for the purpose of receiving a downstream clearance prior to the transfer of control point.

curationApplied.reasoning: The quoted text is a verbatim match and states a shall-strength obligation in an authoritative SERA provision. The claim is an atomic downstream-clearance coordination requirement and is not redundant with the accepted sibling candidates.

sourceUnits.claimText: Aircraft shall maintain the necessary two-way communication with the current air traffic control unit whilst obtaining a downstream clearance.
sourceUnits.rationale: Communication constraint during downstream clearance acquisition.
exactSourceQuotes: Aircraft shall maintain the necessary two-way communication with the current air traffic control unit whilst obtaining a downstream clearance.

sourceUnits.claimText: An aircraft shall be cleared for the entire route to the aerodrome of first intended landing when it has been possible, prior to departure, to coordinate the clearance between all the units under whose control the aircraft will come.
sourceUnits.rationale: Condition for full route clearance based on pre-departure coordination.
exactSourceQuotes: An aircraft shall be cleared for the entire route to the aerodrome of first intended landing: (i) when it has been possible, prior to departure, to coordinate the clearance between all the units under whose control the aircraft will come

sourceUnits.claimText: When coordination as in (2) has not been achieved or is not anticipated, the aircraft shall be cleared only to that point where coordination is reasonably assured; prior to reaching such point, or at such point, the aircraft shall receive further clearance, holding instructions being issued as appropriate.
sourceUnits.rationale: Fallback procedure for partial clearance when full coordination is not possible.
exactSourceQuotes: When coordination as in (2) has not been achieved or is not anticipated, the aircraft shall be cleared only to that point where coordination is reasonably assured; prior to reaching such point, or at such point, the aircraft shall receive further clearance

sourceUnits.claimText: When an aircraft intends to depart from an aerodrome within a control area to enter another control area within a period of thirty minutes, or such other specific period of time as has been agreed between the area control centres concerned, coordination with the subsequent area control centre shall be effected prior to issuance of the departure clearance.
sourceUnits.rationale: Coordination timing requirement for short-duration inter-area flights.
exactSourceQuotes: When an aircraft intends to depart from an aerodrome within a control area to enter another control area within a period of thirty minutes, or such other specific period of time as has been agreed between the area control centres concerned, coordination with the subsequent area control centre shall be effected prior to issuance of the departure clearance.

sourceUnits.claimText: Unless coordinated, downstream clearances shall not affect the aircraft’s original flight profile in any airspace, other than that of the air traffic control unit responsible for the delivery of the downstream clearance.
sourceUnits.rationale: Constraint limiting the scope of uncoordinated downstream clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: Unless coordinated, downstream clearances shall not affect the aircraft’s original flight profile in any airspace, other than that of the air traffic control unit responsible for the delivery of the downstream clearance.

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control clearance shall be coordinated between air traffic control units to cover the entire route of an aircraft or a specified portion thereof.
sourceUnits.rationale: Universal requirement for clearance coordination scope.
exactSourceQuotes: An air traffic control clearance shall be coordinated between air traffic control units to cover the entire route of an aircraft or a specified portion thereof

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control clearance shall be obtained prior to operating a controlled flight, or a portion of a flight as a controlled flight. Such clearance shall be requested through the submission of a flight plan to an air traffic control unit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Conservative candidate from Attempt 1. Attempts 2 and 3 split this into two items. We prefer the single item to avoid fragmentation of a single regulatory sub-clause.
exactSourceQuotes: An air traffic control clearance shall be obtained prior to operating a controlled flight
Such clearance shall be requested through the submission of a flight plan to an air traffic control unit.

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate any necessary instructions or information on other matters such as approach or departure manoeuvres, communications and the time of expiry of the clearance.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(d) and (d)(5) mandating the inclusion of additional necessary instructions/information in clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate:

(5) any necessary instructions or information on other matters such as approach or departure manoeuvres, communi­
cations and the time of expiry of the clearance.

curationApplied.reasoning: Corrected SERA.8015(d) quote to preserve the source soft-hyphen line-break form and promoted it.

manualRepair.reasoning: Corrected SERA.8015(d) quote to preserve the source soft-hyphen line-break form and promoted it.

sourceUnits.claimText: If, prior to departure, it is anticipated that, depending on fuel endurance and subject to reclearance in flight, a decision may be taken to proceed to a revised destination aerodrome, the appropriate air traffic control units shall be so notified by the insertion in the flight plan of information concerning the revised route (where known) and the revised destination.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(b)(4) specifying the pre-departure notification procedure for potential revised destinations.
exactSourceQuotes: If, prior to departure, it is anticipated that, depending on fuel endurance and subject to reclearance in flight, a decision may be taken to proceed to a revised destination aerodrome, the appropriate air traffic control units shall be so notified by the insertion in the flight plan of information concerning the revised route (where known) and the revised destination.

sourceUnits.claimText: The air traffic control clearance relating to the deceleration and descent of an aircraft from supersonic cruise to subsonic flight shall seek to provide for uninterrupted descent at least during the transonic phase.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(c)(2) defining the objective for clearances during supersonic deceleration.
exactSourceQuotes: The air traffic control clearance relating to the deceleration and descent of an aircraft from supersonic cruise to subsonic flight shall seek to provide for uninterrupted descent at least during the transonic phase.

sourceUnits.claimText: The air traffic control clearance relating to the transonic acceleration phase of a supersonic flight shall extend at least to the end of that phase.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(c)(1) defining the temporal scope of clearances for supersonic acceleration.
exactSourceQuotes: The air traffic control clearance relating to the transonic acceleration phase of a supersonic flight shall extend at least to the end of that phase.

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate the clearance limit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(d) and (d)(2) mandating the inclusion of the clearance limit in clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate:
(2) clearance limit;

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate aircraft identification as shown in the flight plan.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(d) and (d)(1) mandating the inclusion of aircraft identification in clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate:
(1) aircraft identification as shown in the flight plan;

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate level(s) of flight for the entire route or part thereof and changes of levels if required.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(d) and (d)(4) mandating the inclusion of flight levels in clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate:
(4) level(s) of flight for the entire route or part thereof and changes of levels if required;

sourceUnits.claimText: Whenever an aircraft has requested a clearance involving priority, a report explaining the necessity for such priority shall be submitted, if requested by the appropriate air traffic control unit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(b)(3) mandating a priority justification report upon ATC request.
exactSourceQuotes: Whenever an aircraft has requested a clearance involving priority, a report explaining the necessity for such priority shall be submitted, if requested by the appropriate air traffic control unit.

sourceUnits.claimText: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate the route of flight.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operative requirement from SERA.8015(d) and (d)(3) mandating the inclusion of the route of flight in clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: An air traffic control clearance shall indicate:
(3) route of flight;

sourceUnits.claimText: An aircraft operated on a controlled aerodrome shall not taxi on the manoeuvring area without clearance from the aerodrome control tower and shall comply with any instructions given by that unit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Conservative candidate from Attempt 1. Attempts 2 and 3 split this. We prefer the single item.
exactSourceQuotes: An aircraft operated on a controlled aerodrome shall not taxi on the manoeuvring area without clearance from the aerodrome control tower
and shall comply with any instructions given by that unit.

sourceUnits.claimText: Air traffic control clearances shall be based solely on the requirements for providing air traffic control service.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from SERA.8015(a) defining the basis for all ATC clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: Air traffic control clearances shall be based solely on the requirements for providing air traffic control service.

sourceUnits.claimText: The pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall inform ATC if an air traffic control clearance is not satisfactory. In such cases, ATC will issue an amended clearance, if practicable.
sourceUnits.rationale: Conservative candidate from Attempt 1. Attempts 2 and 3 split this. We prefer the single item.
exactSourceQuotes: The pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall inform ATC if an air traffic control clearance is not satisfactory.
In such cases, ATC will issue an amended clearance, if practicable.

sourceUnits.claimText: The requirement for an aircraft to maintain an air-ground voice communication watch shall remain in effect when CPDLC has been established.
sourceUnits.rationale: Consistent across all attempts. Clarifies that voice watch obligations persist when CPDLC is active.
exactSourceQuotes: The requirement for an aircraft to maintain an air-ground voice communication watch shall remain in effect when CPDLC has been established.

sourceUnits.claimText: The Member States shall comply with the appropriate provisions on communication failures as have been adopted under the Chicago Convention.
sourceUnits.rationale: Consistent across all attempts. Imposes a compliance obligation on Member States regarding ICAO communication failure provisions.
exactSourceQuotes: The Member States shall comply with the appropriate provisions on communication failures as have been adopted under the Chicago Convention.

sourceUnits.claimText: The Commission shall propose common European procedures by 31 December 2015 at latest, for implementation of the said ICAO provisions in Union law.
sourceUnits.rationale: Only Attempt 1 separates this distinct obligation (Commission's deadline) from the Member States' compliance duty. It is a separate authoritative requirement with a different subject and deadline.
exactSourceQuotes: The Commission shall propose common European procedures by 31 December 2015 at latest, for implementation of the said ICAO provisions in Union law.

sourceUnits.claimText: An aircraft operated as a controlled flight shall maintain continuous air-ground voice communication watch on the appropriate communication channel of, and establish two-way communication as necessary with, the appropriate air traffic control unit, except as may be prescribed by the relevant ANSP in respect of aircraft forming part of aerodrome traffic at a controlled aerodrome.
sourceUnits.rationale: Consistent across all attempts. Direct authoritative requirement for aircraft operators regarding voice watch and two-way communication.
exactSourceQuotes: An aircraft operated as a controlled flight shall maintain continuous air-ground voice communication watch
establish two-way communication as necessary with, the appropriate air traffic control unit

curationApplied.reasoning: The quoted text passes verbatim audit and supports a direct SERA shall-requirement for controlled flights to maintain voice communication watch and establish two-way communication as necessary. The accepted siblings address separate communication-failure/CPDLC provisions and do not make this core requirement redundant.

sourceUnits.claimText: Unless exempted by the competent authority or by the appropriate air traffic services unit under conditions specified by that authority, a controlled flight shall report to the appropriate air traffic services unit, as soon as possible, the time and level of passing each designated compulsory reporting point, together with any other required information.
sourceUnits.rationale: Core obligation for compulsory reporting points. Attempt 3 provides the most complete text by including the exemption clause present in the source sentence.
exactSourceQuotes: Unless exempted by the competent authority or by the appropriate air traffic services unit under conditions specified by that authority, a controlled flight shall report to the appropriate air traffic services unit, as soon as possible, the time and level of passing each designated compulsory reporting point, together with any other required information.

sourceUnits.claimText: Position reports shall similarly be made in relation to additional points when requested by the appropriate air traffic services unit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Obligation to report at additional points upon ATC request. All attempts agree on this distinct requirement.
exactSourceQuotes: Position reports shall similarly be made in relation to additional points when requested by the appropriate air traffic services unit.

sourceUnits.claimText: Controlled flights providing position information to the appropriate air traffic services unit via data link communications shall only provide voice position reports when requested.
sourceUnits.rationale: Exception/limitation for data-link equipped flights regarding voice reporting. All attempts agree on this distinct requirement.
exactSourceQuotes: Controlled flights providing position information to the appropriate air traffic services unit via data link communications shall only provide voice position reports when requested.

sourceUnits.claimText: In the absence of designated reporting points, position reports shall be made at intervals prescribed by the competent authority or specified by the appropriate air traffic services unit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Fallback reporting interval requirement when no designated points exist. All attempts agree on this distinct requirement.
exactSourceQuotes: In the absence of designated reporting points, position reports shall be made at intervals prescribed by the competent authority or specified by the appropriate air traffic services unit.

sourceUnits.claimText: Voice read-back of CPDLC messages shall not be required, unless otherwise specified by the ANSP.
sourceUnits.rationale: Exemption from voice read-back for CPDLC from SERA.923(e)(4). Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: (4) Voice read-back of CPDLC messages shall not be required, unless otherwise specified by the ANSP.

sourceUnits.claimText: The controller shall listen to the read-back to ascertain that the clearance or instruction has been correctly acknowledged by the flight crew and shall take immediate action to correct any discrepancies revealed by the read-back.
sourceUnits.rationale: Controller obligation from SERA.923(e)(3). Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: (3) The controller shall listen to the read-back to ascertain that the clearance or instruction has been correctly acknowledged by the flight crew and shall take immediate action to correct any discrepancies revealed by the read-back.

sourceUnits.rationale: Mandatory read-back item from SERA.923(e)(1)(iv). Consistent across all attempts.

sourceUnits.rationale: Obligation for non-mandatory items from SERA.923(e)(2). All attempts agree on the text and authority. Testability set to sim_executable as the outcome (read-back/acknowledgment) is observable.
exactSourceQuotes: (2) Other clearances or instructions, including conditional clearances and taxi instructions, shall be read back or acknowledged in a manner to clearly indicate that they have been understood and will be complied with.

sourceUnits.claimText: Details of the selected separation minima and of their areas of application shall be notified to pilots and aircraft operators through aeronautical information publications, where separation is based on the use by aircraft of specified navigation aids or specified navigation techniques.
sourceUnits.rationale: All attempts consistently identify the notification obligation to pilots/operators via AIPs as a sub-requirement of (c).
exactSourceQuotes: (c) Details of the selected separation minima and of their areas of application shall be notified:
(2) to pilots and aircraft operators through aeronautical information publications, where separation is based on the use by aircraft of specified navigation aids or specified navigation techniques.

curationApplied.reasoning: The quoted source verbatim supports the atomic obligation to notify pilots and aircraft operators through AIPs under the stated condition. The omitted subparagraph (c)(1) is a separate recipient obligation, not an operative qualification needed to understand this candidate, and the accepted siblings do not redundantly cover it.

sourceUnits.claimText: For traffic that will pass from one into the other of neighbouring airspaces and for routes that are closer to the common boundary of the neighbouring airspaces than the separation minima applicable in the circumstances, the selection of separation minima shall be made in consultation between the ANSPs responsible for the provision of air traffic services in neighbouring airspace.
sourceUnits.rationale: All attempts consistently identify the consultation requirement for ANSPs regarding neighbouring airspace boundaries.
exactSourceQuotes: (b) For traffic that will pass from one into the other of neighbouring airspaces and for routes that are closer to the common boundary of the neighbouring airspaces than the separation minima applicable in the circumstances, the selection of separation minima shall be made in consultation between the ANSPs responsible for the provision of air traffic services in neighbouring airspace.

sourceUnits.claimText: The selection of separation minima for application within a given portion of airspace shall be made by the ANSP responsible for the provision of air traffic services and approved by the competent authority concerned.
sourceUnits.rationale: All attempts consistently identify the ANSP's authority and approval requirement for selecting separation minima.
exactSourceQuotes: (a) The selection of separation minima for application within a given portion of airspace shall be made by the ANSP responsible for the provision of air traffic services and approved by the competent authority concerned.

sourceUnits.claimText: Details of the selected separation minima and of their areas of application shall be notified to the air traffic services units concerned.
sourceUnits.rationale: All attempts consistently identify the notification obligation to ATS units as a sub-requirement of (c).
exactSourceQuotes: (c) Details of the selected separation minima and of their areas of application shall be notified:
(1) to the air traffic services units concerned; and

curationApplied.reasoning: The quoted source verbatim supports the atomic obligation to notify the air traffic services units concerned, with shall-strength inherited from the parent clause. The bundle concern was only that the companion c(2) item was missing, but that item is already present in siblingAccepted, so this candidate is not an unsupported or redundant umbrella.

sourceUnits.claimText: A controlled flight shall, except when landing at a controlled aerodrome, advise the appropriate ATC unit as soon as it ceases to be subject to air traffic control service.
sourceUnits.rationale: All three attempts converge on the same mandatory obligation for controlled flights to advise ATC upon termination of control, with a specific exception for landing at controlled aerodromes. The source text is unambiguous and testable.
exactSourceQuotes: A controlled flight shall, except when landing at a controlled aerodrome, advise the appropriate ATC unit as soon as it ceases to be subject to air traffic control service.
